column3: “Wept a great weeping” is rendered “wept bitterly.”
“On this” is rendered “in spite of this.”
The Hebrew vowels read “the Lord”; NASB reads “my lord.” “Send out” is rendered “put away.”
“The matter is on you” is rendered “this matter is your responsibility,” and “be strong” as “be courageous.”
“Food” is rendered “bread.” “He went there” is rendered “Although he went there”; the meaning is uncertain.
“Open place” is rendered “open square,” and “the rains” as “the heavy rain.”
“So according to your word on us to do” is rendered “That's right! As you have said, so it is our duty to do.”
“The time is rains” is rendered “it is the rainy season.”
“Stand for” is rendered “represent,” and “until to the matter” as “on account of this matter.”
“Stood on this” is rendered “opposed this”; the phrase may also mean they supported it, and the meaning is uncertain.
The Hebrew reads “they separated themselves, Ezra the priest, men”; NASB has “Ezra the priest selected men,” as the ancient versions read.
“Gave their hand” is rendered “pledged”; NASB supplies “they offered.”
NASB reads “Jeremoth,” the name read aloud, for the written “Ramoth.”
